problem:
Consider the boundary value problem

$$
{y}^{″}+25\lambda y=0,\,{y}^{′}(0)={y}^{′}(\pi )=0,\,0\le x\le \pi ,\,\lambda \ge 0.
$$

Find the parameter values corresponding to the eigenvalues and the associated eigenfunctions of this problem.$\,$ The eigenvalues correspond to the parameter values ${\lambda }_{n}=$ {{field-1}}, where $n\in N.$

$\,$ The eigenfunctions are ${y}_{n}(x)=$ {{field-2}}, where ${B}_{n}\in R.$

activity_context.topic_title: Eigenvalues and Eigenfunctions of Homogeneous BVPs

mathematical_indexing_review.source_natural_numbers_convention: unresolved; do not assume N contains zero
mathematical_indexing_review.complete_spectrum: lambda_n=n^2/25 and y_n=B_n cos(nx), n=0,1,2,..., B_n nonzero
mathematical_indexing_review.independent_derivation: At lambda=0, y=Ax+B and both Neumann conditions force A=0, so every nonzero constant is an eigenfunction. At lambda>0, y=A cos(5x sqrt(lambda))+C sin(5x sqrt(lambda)); y'(0)=0 forces C=0. Then y'(pi)=0 forces 5 sqrt(lambda)=n with n a positive integer. Thus lambda=n^2/25 and y=B_n cos(5x sqrt(lambda_n)).
mathematical_indexing_review.choice_proof: The eigenvalue denominators 5,50,10 fail 25 lambda_n=n^2. The frequency-one cosine has residual 24 lambda_n*y. Both sine choices fail the left Neumann condition for a nonzero eigenfunction and lambda_n>0. Frequency-five cosine is the unique displayed correct eigenfunction formula.
